newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN threatens sanctions against Sierra Leone junta.
newsitem.headline: UN threatens sanctions against Sierra Leone junta.

text.p: The Security Council on Wednesday threatened unspecified sanctions against Sierra Leone's coup leaders, which diplomats said could result in an arms and travel ban.
In a statement read at a formal meeting, the Council again condemned the May 25 coup that toppled Sierra Leone's elected government and called for the restoration of civilian rule.
Otherwise, it said it would take "appropriate measures," a diplomatic phrase for sanctions.

Council sources said the measures could include an arms embargo on Sierra Leone as well as a travel ban on members of the junta and some of their supporters. The new government has not been recognised by any country.

"The Security Council will, in the absence of a satisfactory response from the military junta, be ready to take appropriate measures with the objective of restoring the democratically-elected government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah," the statement said.

In the statement, read by Council President Sir John Weston of Britain, the 15-member body said that the junta's attempts to set conditions to restore the Kabbah government were unacceptable and called on it to "renounce its declared intention to remain in power."

The council also said the junta was interfering with the delivery of relief supplies, was threatening civilians and foreigners with violence and had prompted a flow of refugees to neighbouring Guinea where Kabbah is in exile.

West African troops, led by Nigeria, have imposed an air, sea and lande blockade against Sierra Leone. Talks by West African regional leaders broke down on July 30 when junta leader Johnny Paul Koroma said the military would stay in power until the year 2001.
The embargo has already caused severe shortages in Freetown, where most shops and businesses remain closed since the coup which was followed by massive looting.
